channel.title: TheAttn
channel.description: Science, space and technology news from TheAttn.

item.title: Shadows of Division: How Israel’s Separation Wall Compares to the Berlin Wall
Blood on the Streets: Over $2 Trillion Wiped Out in One Day as Post-Election Panic Grips Wall Street
item.description: The Nasdaq crashed 5.52% and the S&P 500 fell 4.36% in their worst day since April 2025, as fears of an AI crackdown under a Democratic Congress triggered a global sell-off.

item.title: Teeth That Heal Themselves? Scientists Regrow Real Enamel With a Fluoride-Free Gel
item.description: Once enamel is gone, it is gone for good. A protein gel from the University of Nottingham just rebuilt it in the lab, and a first product is already heading for human testing.

item.title: Living drugs: the promise and pitfalls of CAR T-cell therapy
item.description: CAR T-cell therapy turns a patient's own immune cells into a precision weapon against cancer, but toxicity, cost and manufacturing delays still limit who can benefit.

item.title: Pakistan launches PKR 16 billion Pasban scheme to reward formal remittances
item.description: The State Bank of Pakistan and the Pakistan Banks Association have launched a bank-funded rewards scheme with quarterly cash draws to steer remittances away from hundi and hawala.

item.title: Canva Announces Major Restructure Affecting Nearly 1,300 Roles Amid Tech Squeeze
item.description: Australian design software giant Canva restructures its workforce, cutting roughly 22% of roles to flatten management and manage rising compute costs associated with AI capabilities.

item.title: Blue Wave Sweeps Midterms: Democrats Seize The House
item.description: Democrats are projected to win both the Senate and the House in the 3 November midterms, and flipped governor's mansions in Texas, Georgia, Ohio and Iowa.

item.title: China finds a real-life “Three-Body” star system: a dead star spinning 300 times a second
item.description: Astronomers using the FAST telescope found a pulsar locked in a stable dance with a white dwarf and a Sun-like star, and the third star explains why the pulsar is slowing down so oddly.

item.title: Psyllium husk cut LDL cholesterol by 13 points across 28 trials, and it doesn’t work the way you think
item.description: A review of 28 randomized trials found about 10 grams of psyllium a day lowered LDL by roughly 13 mg/dL. The secret is a gel in your gut that traps bile acids, not anything the body absorbs.

item.title: Cholesterol drug ezetimibe linked to lower dementia risk in study, but trials are needed
item.description: Researchers at the University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences found that ezetimibe, a common cholesterol drug, was associated with far lower Alzheimer's and dementia rates in patient records. The finding is observational and not yet proven in trials.

item.title: US aid to Israel since 1948 totals about $300 billion, adjusted for inflation
item.description: Israel is the largest cumulative recipient of US foreign aid since World War II. Here is what the numbers show, what the current agreement guarantees, and where supporters and critics disagree.

item.title: South Africa’s Silent Exports: How Mid-Century Innovation Reshaped Global Engineering and Medicine
item.description: From the dolos breakwater blocks on Lake Erie to the first heart transplant, South African inventions of the mid-20th century quietly shaped engineering, medicine, mining and everyday life worldwide.

item.title: Common Anti-Diarrhea Drug Loperamide Can Trigger Self-Destruction in Brain Cancer Cells
item.description: Lab research from Goethe University Frankfurt found that loperamide, the active ingredient in Imodium, pushes glioblastoma cells into self-destruction. Experts stress it is not a cure.

item.title: Australian Actor Richard Norton’s Death Triggered by Unapproved Peptide Injections, Coroner Rules
item.description: A Victorian coroner has ruled that actor and stuntman Richard Norton died from anaphylaxis and cardiac arrest after self-administering unapproved peptides.

item.title: Columbia Engineers Develop Implantable Smart Stent to Detect and Electrocute Circulating Cancer Cells
item.description: Columbia biomedical engineers have unveiled the Stentinel, an implantable device that catches and destroys circulating tumor cells in the bloodstream before they can seed secondary tumors.

item.title: Alphabet suffers worst day ever as AI spending turns cash flow negative
item.description: Shares in Google's parent fell nearly 13%, wiping out about $500 billion in value, after a third-quarter miss on earnings, weaker search growth and a $9.07 billion cash outflow.

item.title: Scripps study explores biweekly GLP-1 dosing for weight loss maintenance
item.description: Early data from Scripps Clinic suggests some patients may keep their weight off after stretching GLP-1 injections from weekly to every two weeks, but experts warn the study is small and uncontrolled.

item.title: Retatrutide explained: approval status, how it works, trial results and side effects
item.description: Retatrutide is an investigational weekly injection from Eli Lilly that targets three hormone receptors. It is not yet approved anywhere, and Lilly plans to apply to the FDA in early 2027.

item.title: Frog Gut Bacteria Eliminates Colorectal Tumors in Mice With 100% Success Rate
item.description: Researchers at JAIST successfully eliminated colorectal tumors in mice using a single injection of Ewingella americana, a bacterium isolated from Japanese tree frogs.

item.title: Could GLP-1 drugs be anti-aging medications?
item.description: Early research suggests GLP-1 medications like semaglutide and tirzepatide may slow biological aging, extending health span beyond just weight loss and blood sugar control.

item.title: Israel elections: No majority win as Netanyahu, Eisenkot tied at 51 seats
item.description: Israel’s opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot vowed to quickly form a government after neither bloc secured a clear majority, while Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu alleged electoral fraud.

item.title: Mecca pact officials in Tehran
item.description: One or two sentences shown on the card and under the headline.

item.title: The Attn: Lula wins fourth term in Brazil after comeback runoff victory
item.description: Brazil's president beat Flavio Bolsonaro by more than four million votes, but a challenge to the result and a hostile Congress lie ahead.
